reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and for our side (Customer) the absence of any vendor audit/inspection/verification right is at least as favorable as the playbook's preferred position, so no redline or counterparty comment is required.

Cited paragraphs are consistent with the rationale: § 3 Restrictions on Use (including (e)) imposes substantive use limits only, with no compliance-audit, reporting, records-inspection or system-access mechanism, and § 20 General Matters covers unrelated boilerplate.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected here: it is a heuristic looking for frequency/notice/cost caps, which cannot appear where no audit clause exists, and does not indicate an incorrect verdict.
Correctly declines to insert audit machinery, which would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Vendor rights beyond the current contract — appropriately the smallest (zero) edit.

Retained as internal evidence only; if a usage-verification or true-up right appears elsewhere in the agreement (e.g., in fee or reporting schedules not cited here), the AUDIT limits would need to be added, so this conclusion is contingent on the full-document search described.
